subject: Immediate keystone rollforward: short-notice hotfix and mitigation steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
To: emily.rodgers@acme-analytics.com, james.brooks@acme-analytics.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.inference.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 03:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate keystone rollforward: short-notice hotfix and mitigation steps

Hi Emily / James —

Quick heads-up: we identified a correctness regression in the keystone KV-shard mapping that can cause transient model-decoding errors for sequences >8k tokens under particular load patterns. The issue has a low rate in practice but we decided to apply an unscheduled rollforward to remove the faulty routing case.

Planned change (starting immediately):
- Deploy keystone hotfix to the serving fleet in two waves (canary -> global).
- Canary window: 15 minutes, targeted on 5% of traffic, then expand to 100% if metrics are clean.
- If we observe decoder errors >0.1% or latency regressions >10% we will automatically trigger a controlled rollback.

What this means for Acme: short maintenance window with potential for ~10-30s connection glitches for in-flight streaming responses; we do not expect data loss. We will keep your requests routed to alternative regions if you have cross-region fallback enabled.

Immediate asks from you:
1) If you have any high-priority jobs running in the next hour that cannot tolerate transient failures, please pause them now or reply with "PAUSE" and we will throttle traffic from your org for the rollout window.
2) Confirm whether your account uses regional affinity only in us-west-2 or also has us-east-1 fallback.

Attachments: keystone-hotfix.patch (diff) and rollback plan attached for your review.

I will post minute-by-minute updates in this thread and on the incident page: https://drive.redwood.com/incident/keystone-hotfix-20270630

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the fast action. Two quick questions:

1) Can you confirm whether streaming sessions already established will be retried automatically or will they error back to our clients? We have a batch of long-running streams started around 02:30 PDT.
2) If we request throttling for our account, what is the expected effect on queued inference jobs vs. real-time chat traffic?

If there's a safe time to resume our morning run I can schedule it, otherwise we'll send PAUSE.

—Emily

Subject: Re: Immediate keystone rollforward: short-notice hotfix and mitigation steps

Marcus — internal runbook actions below (summarized). I'm copying CustOps and the Deploy team.

Runbook (executed):
- 03:20 PDT: Patch built and smoke-tested on staging (keystone-hotfix.patch).
- 03:40 PDT: Canary fleet deployed (5%): monitoring hooks started; no immediate errors observed.
- 03:55 PDT: Detected small spike in decoder WARNs (0.03%), below threshold; canary expanded to 30%.
- 04:10 PDT: Expanded to 100% after latency and error signals stable.

Customer mitigation:
- For Acme (per Marcus): we applied temporary traffic shaping to reduce long-polling stream concurrency; this should prevent their queued jobs from being dropped but increase queue latency by ~2-3s.
- If Acme requests PAUSE: we will redirect all traffic from their org to a warm fallback pool in us-east-1 with slightly higher token egress cost but stable decoding.

Attachments: rollback plan attached to this thread. If we need to rollback we will follow the exact step sequence in keystone-rollback-plan.pdf (pre-approved by SRE leads).

Next actions:
- Karthik: confirm that the warm fallback pool is fully warmed and available (ETA 10m).
- Stephanie: coordinate an update to Acme and confirm whether they want to PAUSE.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Production Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Immediate keystone rollforward: short-notice hotfix and mitigation steps

Emily / James —

Thank you for the patience and the quick confirm on your side. Summary and follow-up:

1) Streaming behavior: established streams that experienced transient decoder errors were retried by our client proxies where possible. A small percentage (~0.08%) returned an error to the client and will need a client-side retry. We are adding automatic idempotent retry guidance to the postmortem (link below).

2) Throttling effect: when Acme requested throttling we redirected your traffic to the warm fallback pool in us-east-1 as discussed. Queued batch jobs were held and executed with slightly increased queue latency (~3s median) rather than being dropped. Real-time chat requests remained prioritized but experienced some added tail latency.

3) Rollback: not required. Metrics show error rates returned to baseline after the rollforward and latency impact was within the tolerance defined in the canary policy.

Next steps and links:
- Postmortem write-up (draft): https://drive.redwood.com/incident/keystone-hotfix-20270630/postmortem-draft
- Action item: we will ship a patch to the client proxy that adds an explicit idempotent-retry header recommendation by 2027-07-07.
- If you prefer a formal postmortem call, I can schedule a 30-minute sync this week.

Apologies for the short notice; we prioritized removing the regression quickly to avoid a larger customer impact. Please reply if you'd like us to schedule the postmortem call.

Best,
—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
